This script is cleared as a live classical Fift caller, while the remaining retained Fift callers keep this question OPEN. single-nominator-pool's contract and tosctl operator command are converted; the old Fift operator file was moved to a test-only legacy fixture at T05. merkle-base-state-mismatch.closure_condition: A run-evidenced diagnosis identifies whether the mismatched candidate state_update and base state are selected by production consensus or by the test fixture, followed by a guard that fails when that demonstrated ordering is reintroduced.
merkle-base-state-mismatch.observation: Two recovered test-consensus-simplex2-pq-finality-e2e-100 errors under whole-suite parallel load show the same one-height mismatch. At 68ea21db4 on 2026-09-22 07:02:35 UTC, StateResolver actors 87 and 77 reported expected fixture state seqno 5 but applied to seqno 4; at efd22ce46 on 2026-09-22 12:46:23 UTC, actor 83 reported expected seqno 23 but applied to seqno 22. The four hashes were independently decoded, but original candidate IDs, BOCs and stacks were not retained. Production defect mechanism: StateResolver's QuerySlotSkipped shortcut could replace a signed candidate's exact parent with available_base. At bc379ec2c the resolver was changed to resolve the exact CandidateId. The actor regression at 1a2f33940 reproduces both original hash pairs under delayed local NotarCert(P) persistence; 528f0864e additionally reproduces them when only a peer holds NotarCert(P) and real Consensus::start_generation triggers resolution. Pre-fix red and fixed green each passed 40/40 for each ordering, with controls, bounded notready and cross-checks recorded in N6-MERKLE-REPRO-20260923.md. On 1e192efce the three branch CI jobs passed and the fixed actor tests passed independently in ordinary Release. This proves a production path can cause and the patch prevents the observed mismatch shape; it does not uniquely attribute either September failure to that path. Keep the incident OPEN for explicit historical attribution and integration-tree disposition.

pq-validator-set-installation-parity.observation: C01 identified a source-level ADNL uniqueness mismatch. C07 independently ran the old config contract against a duplicate-ADNL set: the contract returned VALIDATOR_SET_INSTALLED while the node decoder rejected the same BOC; no live chain was halted. On the local repair tree, a compiled-contract sandbox also showed that a set above the node's UINT64_MAX/3 total-weight cap was installed. check_validator_set now refuses both, with old-red/new-green tests and an Elector-produced duplicate-ADNL set negative. The separate validator-governed install_param route still calls valid_live_validator_set_limits?, which checks counts but not complete descriptor identity and weight rules before writing ConfigParam 34-37. Therefore the whole installation-parity question remains OPEN; neither C01 nor the Elector-route repair is an observed masterchain halt.

pool-first-stake-birth-witness-missing.observation: At discovery, both launch-facing pool callers obtained node-bound PQ authorization but called nominator::new_stake, which fixed the optional controller birth witness to None; the Elector returns reason 8 for such a first stake. They now share an optional NodeBinding locator for the original deployment StateInit BOC and a builder that compares node authorization, pool controller identity and live ConfigParam 47 dictionary membership before emitting a witnessed pool order. Missing and mismatched inputs refuse locally in tests. Old configurations remain readable but cannot first-stake without this public artifact. The config bind import-birth command extracts the public StateInit from an operator-supplied deployment transaction BOC, verifies its transaction account, message destination and derived identity against the configured controller, and binds a create-new artifact to an idle node. This is offline shape/identity verification, not independent chain-finality proof; deployment commands still do not create or retain the controller birth artifact. Report SHA-256 b5a448040fd75f5f55e206751f86831cf68b3c2de5d3f84fdca236e2447a693d; see T3-CONFIG-WALLET-FIRST-STAKE-DIAGNOSTIC.md. The two caller outcomes satisfy this first-stake witness question, independently of the retained Fift inventory and liquid-staking exclusion. Liquid staking remains outside the launch set.
pool-first-stake-birth-witness-missing.t3_handoff_plan: Retain the controller deployment transaction BOC and import its original StateInit through config bind import-birth; current mutable account data is not a birth artifact. Both product callers read the bound artifact, compare it with node and pool identity, require code membership in live ConfigParam 47 and build through the shared verified witness path before wallet send.
